title: When Need Exceeds Support: Lower Medicaid Reimbursement for Cleft Orthodontia in High Pediatric Enrollment States.
source: PubMed · The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
byline: McCall RR, Elver A, West JD, et al.
html: ObjectiveTo analyze the association between Medicaid provider reimbursement for cleft lip and palate (CL/P) procedures and state-level economic factors.DesignCross-sectional study of publicly available 2025 state Medicaid provider reimbursement rates associated with CL/P procedures. Statistical analysis compared provider reimbursement and demographic factors.SettingNational sample of Medicaid reimbursement fee schedules.ParticipantsFifty U.S. states utilizing fee-for-service reimbursement.Main Outcome Measure(s)Reimbursement Rates for D8020 (Phase I: Limited Orthodontia, Transitional Dentition) and D8080 (Phase II: Comprehensive Orthodontia, Adolescent Dentition), CPT 42210 (Palatoplasty for Cleft Palate with Bone Graft), Pediatric Population of Medicaid and Children's Health Insurance Program.ResultsD8080 reimbursement was negatively correlated with pediatric Medicaid enrollment ( r = -0.375, p = 0.014). Multivariate linear regression predicted D8080 reimbursement, explaining 46.9% of variance (adjusted R 2 = 0.41). Higher reimbursement was associated with higher cost of living (β = 0.39, p = 0.007), poverty (β = 0.51, p < 0.001), and Medicaid expansion (β = 0.27, p = 0.041), but lower in states with greater pediatric enrollment (β = -0.53, p < 0.001).ConclusionsMedicaid provider reimbursement for comprehensive orthodontic treatment is independently associated with state socioeconomic characteristics. Reimbursement decreased with higher enrollment. This trend may further limit provider availability for low-income families with existing barriers in access to care. These findings suggest that Medicaid reimbursement may not adequately scale with pediatric beneficiary demand, potentially limiting access to multidisciplinary treatment.
